LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, how to watch, what to know and a prediction before the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup Getty Images In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts . Houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot. The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline. Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Follow the game live here Where to watch Texans vs. Colts live Date: Thursday, Nov. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: NRG Stadium (Houston) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Texans -12.5, O/U 44.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Colts have the ball The Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces. Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing. Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL . Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions. The Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell , Ashton Dulin , Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games. The Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor 's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan , including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up. Taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state. When the Texans have the ball C.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season. The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner , either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins. It's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence. This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense. I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. The Bengals are 6-2 SU and 6-1-1 ATS in their last eight road games and have scored at least 30 points in three straight on the road. (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Texans vs. Browns in NFL Week 10) Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE The Cleveland Browns will get their starting quarterback back in action in Week 10 against the Houston Texans, as Deshaun Watson is off the injury report and set to start. Watson (concussion) missed the team's Week 9 loss to the New Orleans Saints, though backup Shedeur Sanders played pretty decently in his place. Sanders helped get the Browns to overtime, where they lost on a two-point attempt. The second-year quarterback finished the day with 297 passing yards and two scores, carrying the ball for 28 yards on 10 attempts as well. Still, Todd Monken named Watson the starter for Week 10, as the veteran has led the team to a 5-3 record in eight starts with five fourth quarter comeback wins. In the 2026 season, Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven scores and three interceptions. He's also carried the ball 51 times for 217 yards and a score. He's playing a revenge game against his former team -- Houston -- in Week 10. Even with Watson back, oddsmakers aren't buying the 5-4 Browns in this matchup. They are 4.5-point underdogs at home in the latest odds at DraftKings , even though they have a better record than an underachieving Houston team so far in 2026. Watson is looking to have a big game to keep the starting job, as it's possible the Browns could turn back to Sanders if things go south. Cleveland is still in the playoff picture in the AFC, but it has taken a step back with two straight losses to Pittsburgh and New Orleans. The Dolphins face their AFC East rivals, the Buffalo Bills, on the road this weekend, a game that features a team tied for the worst record in the AFC visiting the team with the best record in the conference. Division games are typically closer than expected, but this one might be the exception that proves the rule. Miami is relying on rookies and first-year players across the roster this year, including quarterback Kyle McCord. An undrafted rookie in 2025, McCord spent his entire rookie season on the Philadelphia Eagles' practice squad. He looked composed last week against the Colts and he will look to carry that into Week 11. The good news for McCord and the Dolphins' offense is Buffalo's pass defense ranks just 28th in the league, allowing 241.9 passing yards per game. Miami faces a tough battle this week, but they are also a team that has played tough all season. They may have only won one of their first nine games, but they have competed in most of them, and they are clearly growing as the complete franchise rebuild progresses into the second half of the year. The Dolphins are 16.5-point underdogs for Sunday, a line that has held fairly steady throughout the week. The moneyline has Buffalo at -1,600 to win straight up, while the Dolphins are +900. The combined point total is 44.5. Each week, our contributors make their straight-up winner predictions for every game on the schedule. Buffalo has started the year 8-1, sitting atop the AFC East and the AFC as a whole at this time. The Bills have used a strong offensive attack to lead the way, with quarterback Josh Allen gunning for another MVP award. But Allen is more focused on team success, rather than going after any personal accomplishments this season. Allen's focus is on helping the Bills take home the Super Bowl trophy this year, and this entire team feels different this time around. There is still a lot of work to do for this Bills team, with areas that the group can improve on as the year moves forward. But overall, Buffalo's year couldn't have started much better than it already has. As for the upcoming week, Buffalo will be hosting the Miami Dolphins , giving them another chance to grab a win. Miami has struggled this year, going 1-8 for the year so far. The Dolphins will be starting quarterback Kyle McCord again this week, with normal starter Malik Willis injured. McCord threw for 209 yards last week in a loss to the Indianapolis Colts, and the Bills will attempt to throw him off his game. NFL experts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report made game predictions for each matchup on the schedule this week. Within this, only four of the seven analysts went with the Bills to take down the Dolphins at home. Davenport, Hanford, Knox, and Sobleski were the four to choose the Bills to win, which is a little surprising entering the game. But the Bills will try to grab another win, moving closer to a division title. Given where the two teams are, only having a little over half take Buffalo is interesting, but likely speaks to where Miami is. While the Dolphins haven't been winning games, the team has been competitive all season. Buffalo also has a massive game upcoming next week against the Kansas City Chiefs, and the team could be lacking focus. Oftentimes, games like this could be traps for teams, and the Bills will need to avoid overlooking the Dolphins. Kickoff for the game between the Bills and the Dolphins is scheduled for 10:00 a.m. PT/1:00 p.m. ET.

away.headline: Buffalo Bills vs. Miami Dolphins injury news: Ed Oliver questionable for Week 11
away.blurb: Oliver is now listed as questionable for Sunday’s home game, though the news is not all doom and gloom. Matt Parrino provided some context to Oliver’s injury , tweeting that “(p)er a league source, Ed Oliver notified Bills training staff this morning that he felt pain in his oblique. The staff checked it out and there’s optimism that he’ll play against the Dolphins.” Per NFL rules, Oliver’s ailment must be accounted for on the injury report even at this late stage, which is why he’s being listed as questionable. In the past, Oliver’s situation would have likely had him tabbed as “probable” for game day. The NFL has since done away with that injury designation, which has seen the questionable term pick up the slack in filing injuries throughout the league. Should Oliver be unable to go (or limited in some fashion) it would be a huge blow to Buffalo’s defense, which already has to account for injuries to starters in cornerback Christian Benford and inside linebacker Dorian Williams. Both Bills defenders have been ruled out ahead of Week 11 . The injuries continue piling up for the Buffalo Bills ahead of their Week 11 home game against the Miami Dolphins. A surprise report originating from the team on Saturday afternoon revealed that Bills starting defensive tackle Ed Oliver is dealing with an oblique injury.

away.headline: Key Linebacker Injury Gives Bills' Rookie Fourth-Rounder Shot to Shine vs. Dolphins
away.blurb: Starting linebacker Dorian Williams was ruled out for Sunday's contest with a calf injury, which should thrust fourth-round pick Kaleb Elarms-Orr into a starting role opposite veteran Terrel Bernard. Out of Buffalo's 600 defensive snaps in 2026, Elarms-Orr has seen the field in 126, or 21%, of them, working behind Williams and Bernard and fighting with Joe Andreessen for the right to see the field. Coming out of college, Elarms-Orr was praised for his athleticism, which included a 4.47 40-yard dash, a 40-inch vertical jump and a 4.41 shuttle run, and college production, as he l ed the Big 12 with 130 tackles in 2025. Bills' Updated Week 11 Injury Report: Christian Benford, Dalton Kincaid Remain Out The Buffalo Bills ' final injury report for their Week 11 matchup against the Miami Dolphins was released on Friday, and one of the inactives presents an opportunity for an under-the-radar member of the Bills' rookie class. While Miami does not look like a challenging opponent, a strong outing from the TCU product will go a long way toward ensuring this game is not a trap game with a gauntlet awaiting them starting Thursday. What has Kaleb Elarms-Orr done in 2026? Statistically, the rookie has tallied 18 tackles, a pass defended and two fumble recoveries, showcasing his athleticism in spurts, but he'll have a chance to make himself known to Bills Mafia in front of the Highmark Stadium crowd on Sunday. In the preseason, Elarms-Orr tallied six tackles and turned heads in training camp, most notably by starting a fight that drew the attention of veterans, including guard Alec Anderson. "Shoutout to the rookie linebacker Kaleb [Elarms-Orr]," Anderson said after the fight. "You'd rather say 'chill' than 'sic 'em'... that's a good thing." “Elarms-Orr is a well-built linebacker with above-average athleticism but problematic instincts,” NFL.com ’s Lance Zierlein wrote. “He has the speed and athleticism to get to the football from sideline to sideline.” The Hayward, California native will need to combine his speed with improved instincts if he is to help Buffalo shut down Miami's playmakers. Elarms-Orr will be relieved to not go up against running back De'Von Achane, who ran for 1,350 yards, good for fifth in the league, and also led the Dolphins with 67 receptions. Achane tore his ACL in Week 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs. Second-year running back Ollie Gordon II, Achane's replacement, has run for at least 100 yards in two of six games since Achane's injury, and the running game will be key for Miami if it is to keep the ball away from Josh Allen and the Bills' offense. When quarterback Kyle McCord drops back to throw , tight end Greg Dulcich, who has 24 catches for 270 yards this season, will be his main responsibility. With a short week coming up, a strong performance from Elarms-Orr could be exactly what the Bills welcome. away.headline: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published Nov 18, 2026 ALAIN POUPART Ala

home.headline: Is Garrett Wilson Playing Today? (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Bills vs. Jets in NFL Week 10)
home.blurb: Wilson is officially listed as questionable for the AFC East battle with the Buffalo Bills, but he appears to be trending in the right direction to play. Garrett Wilson (concussion) officially listed questionable for Week 10. According to Jets head coach Aaron Glenn, Wilson needs to clear one more step to get out of the consussion protocol, but Glenn believes that will happen in time for Sunday's game. Last week, New York scored just 12 points with Wilson out of the lineup, and it slipped to 16th in the league in EPA/Play on offense as a result. This season, Wilson has appeared in eight of the Jets' nine games, catching 43 passes for 527 yards and three scores. He's played 88.5 percent of the team's offensive snaps, so he'll be out there for almost every play against Buffalo if he's able to go. The Jets are banged up across the board at receiver, as Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. are all listed as questionable. Still, the former first-round pick has been one of the better receivers in the league since being drafted, and he’ll clearly be the go-to option against a shaky Buffalo secondary as long as he plays. Carl Granderson and the Saints' pass rush get a 7-2 Chicago Bears team coming off its bye, with kickoff set for noon CT on FOX. New Orleans will be shorthanded up front. Center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga missed practice again Thursday, according to the Saints injury report , and Kellen Moore said Asim Richards will miss a few weeks with a knee injury. Here are four bold predictions for how the Saints pull the upset anyway. Carl Granderson and Chase Young combine for three sacks Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints defensive end Chase Young (99) reacts to a play against the Cleveland Browns during the first quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Granderson has 8.5 sacks and Young has eight, and the two of them have carried the pass rush all season. Against Carolina, Granderson had seven pressures and Young had five, according to PFF . Set that next to what Chicago has allowed. Caleb Williams has been sacked 14 times in six games, while the Saints' two edge rushers have 16.5 sacks between them. Chicago's Super Bowl hopes depend on Williams staying upright. Three sacks between Granderson and Young keep this a low-scoring game, which is the only kind New Orleans can win. Saints hold the Bears under 100 rushing yards Oct 19, 2025; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (4) runs the ball against New Orleans Saints safety Jonas Sanker (33) and linebacker Pete Werner (20) during the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images The Bears average 142 rushing yards per game. D'Andre Swift leads them with 576 yards and 10 touchdowns, and Kyle Monangai, a full participant this week after a toe injury, has averaged 5.4 yards per carry. New Orleans has been better against the run since its bye. Cleveland and Carolina combined for 192 yards on 66 carries, 2.9 per attempt, according to the Saints' team site . "From a big-picture perspective, felt like controlling their run game was important, I felt like we did that," Moore said Monday. Linebacker Pete Werner, who leads the team with 70 tackles, missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a hamstring injury, which makes this one bolder. Kaden Elliss had seven stops against Carolina, and he'll have to clean up the middle if Werner can't go. Jordyn Tyson catches his first NFL touchdown Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (0) dives for the sideline with Cleveland Browns cornerback Myles Harden (26) defending during the fourth quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn ImagesMatthew Hinton-Imagn Images The rookie has taken over Bryce Lance's snaps , and he has 15 catches for 110 yards in two games. When Carolina took away Chris Olave , Tyson became Tyler Shough's top target. He's still looking for his first touchdown, and he was limited Wednesday and Thursday with a chest injury. If he plays, the red zone is where it happens. New Orleans has scored touchdowns on 72.4% of its red-zone trips, and Chicago will spend plenty of attention on Olave. Saints intercept Caleb Williams twice Oct 11, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints safety Jonas Sanker (7) steals the ball and runs it in for a touchdown against Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Tai Felton (13) during the second half at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images New Orleans has four interceptions all season, which is what makes this one bold. Julian Blackmon and Martin Emerson Jr. have two apiece, and Emerson missed practice Wednesday and Thursday with a concussion. Williams has thrown five interceptions in six games, and Bears quarterbacks have nine as a team. Chicago is minus-4 in turnover margin and New Orleans is minus-8, according to the Saints' game preview . Some Bears fans already see a trap game here. away.headline: New Orleans Saints injury report: Five ruled out; Tyson good to go
away.blurb: The Saints will be without five players Sunday at Soldier Field, and the list hits the offensive line and the secondary hardest. New Orleans ruled out center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), tackle Asim Richards (knee), cornerback Martin Emerson (concussion), and safety Justin Reid (personal matter). None of the five practiced at all this week, so none of these come as a surprise, and Reid’s personal matter is the technical term for him being released by the team. The offensive line losses stand out most. Three linemen are out, including McCoy and Fuaga, and that’s a lot of reshuffling up front against a Bears defense that sacked Baker Mayfield four times in its last game. The back end is banged up, too. With Emerson and Reid out, cornerback Decamerion Richardson (thigh) is questionable after being limited all week. Linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) is also questionable, even though he didn’t practice once after leaving the Carolina game. Questionable after three missed practices usually leans toward sitting, so I wouldn’t count on Werner. Either way, Caleb Williams should see a thinner coverage group than usual. The Saints did get some good news. Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest) was upgraded to a full practice Friday after two limited days. Alvin Kamara practiced fully after a rest day Wednesday, and running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) fully participated all week. All three carry no game designation. Linebacker Isaiah Stalbird missed Friday’s practice for a personal matter but also has no designation. The New Orleans Saints submitted their final injury report of the week on Thursday ahead of their Week 11 contest with the Chicago Bears. away.headline: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears
away.blurb: Sheesh. The New Orleans Saints (3-6) shared a lengthy injury report ahead of Sunday's game with the Chicago Bears (7-2), with seven players not participating and two other limited to start the week. They'll need all hands on deck for a chance at upsetting one of the hottest teams in the NFL. Let's hope they can get it done. And let's start with the good news. Rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) returned to full practice reps on Wednesday after missing several games between that shoulder injury and a stint in concussion protocol. We haven't seen him since the rookie exited Week 9's game in Paris against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Donaldson has been a productive rusher for New Orleans on limited snaps (averaging 4.8 yards per carry and a team-high 64.7% success rate), and he was just starting to earn a bigger role after initially getting on the field as a short-yardage specialist. He competes hard in pass protection, too. How snaps could be divided between him, Travis Etienne Jr., Alvin Kamara (more on him in a minute), and Audric Estime remains to be seen. What about those seven players who didn't practice? We expected Kamara (not injury related) would get his usual rest day, which has been a pattern since he suffered a Week 5 back injury. He turned 31 this summer and has worn a lot of tread off his tires so it makes sense to give him a lighter workload during the week, especially if he's going to have a reduced role on game days. Kamara was only on the field last Sunday for 16 snaps but he scored two touchdowns. Veteran safety Justin Reid (not injury related) did not practice on Wednesday due to a personal matter, and head coach Kellen Moore was noncommittal when asked if Reid was expected back on Thursday. Stay tuned. Backup right tackle Asim Richards (knee) and a couple of defensive starters who got nicked up against the Carolina Panthers -- cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) -- were held out of practice. Additionally, starting right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee) and center Erik McCoy (biceps) both did not practice, though Moore said "we'll see" if either of them can return to work later this week. Two other players were limited to start the week: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest), who you can read more about here ; and backup corner Decamerion Richardson (thigh). We'll be watching for updates on their status as the week continues. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears

home.headline: Final Injury Report: Saints-Bears, Plus Reid Officially Gone
home.source: New Orleans Saints On SI on MSN
home.blurb: Cornerback Martin Emerson - concussion OUT Tackle Taliese Fuaga - knee injury OUT Center Eric McCoy - biceps injury OUT Safety Justin Reid - covered above OUT (obviously) Tackle Asim Richards - bum knee OUT Linebacker Pete Werner - hamstring QUESTIONABLE - Emerson will be in concussion protocol and has been ruled out for Sunday - McCoy's injury will take two-to-three weeks to heal, not enough to put on the IR. He has been declared out for Sunday . - Richards is in the same boat as McCoy, except he's a week ahead. He has been ruled officially out for Sunday. - Werner's hammie is not officially out for Sunday, instead he is listed as questionable . Cornerback Decamerion Richardson - thigh QUESTIONABLE With the absence of Emerson now official, Richardson's limited participation all week looks to be a good sign that the third year man, formerly with Las Vegas, will be able to fill a role this weekend. Cornerback Kyler Gordon - shoulder OUT Wide receiver Zavion Thomas - ankle QUESTIONABLE - Gordon was considered day-to-day after going down with the injured shoulder against Tampa Bay a week and a half ago. He will be sitting out the Saints game with a short work week for Chicago, who will be playing on Thanksgiving Day against the Lions. - Thomas was not listed on the Bears' injury report until Friday when he showed up as not taking part in practice. His game status is officially questionable . Out of those four, Simmons was the only player listed as limited all week until Friday. Saints Stock Down Report: Moore Running Out of Excuses Ahead of Bears Matchup While the Saints and Bears posted their final injury report of the week before their game at Noon on Sunday at Soldier Field, New Orleans finished its business with veteran safety Justin Reid . The Louisiana native made it official from his standpoint late Thursday morning. Then the Saints followed with their posting a little over 3-and-a-half hours later. This story took almost a day and a half to come to a conclusion after the Internet went abuzz with the imminent news of Reid's departure . Expect Saints' fourth year man Jordan Howden to step into the gap left by Reid. Howden has seen his playing time pick up over the last few weeks. There was some movement among those on the Saints practice list on Friday. Much like what we saw Wednesday and Monday, Running back CJ Donaldson - shoulder Running back Alvin Kamara - not injury related on Wednesday. It was a day of rest. Wide receiver Jordyn Tyson - chest All three have been ruled as game-ready for Sunday. The Bears injury report was half as long as the Saints and not nearly as severe. Wide receiver Luther Burden - Concussion Running back Kyle Monangai - Toe Cornerback Malik Muhammad - Toe Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons - knee Wednesdays, On SI Saints will answer your questions about what we see from our vantage point. I did that the past two weeks. After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow. The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14 Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well. Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13 Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Carolina Panthers Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close. Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22 New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers (-3.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17 Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (-3) In Mexico, Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders (+6.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. Pick: Bengals 34, Commanders 30 Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap. On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there. The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win. Won't: Titans' defense continues downward spiral However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games. If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason. Dallas is a veteran-led group in the middle of a difficult year; their down season can't be compared to that of the Titans, and QB Dak Prescott is sure to run this defense through the ringer. On the road after arguably their worst showing of the year, Saleh's defense has their back against the wall. Prediction: Titans win, 30-27 With that said, I still think the Titans find a way to pull this one out. If the away team can strike a balance between their growing offensive attack and a defense that isn't allowing Dallas to do whatever they want, a close win is in the cards. The Titans have yet to play a full, complete game this year. Even their Week 6 victory over the Indianapolis Colts saw Tennessee trailing 13-0 at halftime. I'm predicting that the Titans get this done, and do so by offering a solid showing through all four quarters. That means a consistent Cam Ward, a defense that bends, but doesn't break, reliable play-calling on either side of the ball, and at least a little good luck on the injury front. A lot has to go right, but this game wouldn't have been seen as winnable only a few short weeks ago. For that reason, I believe the Titans will win it. away.blurb: Spears is nursing a nagging knee injury and will miss at least the Titans' next four games. He also sat out Tennessee's games in Weeks 7 and 8 due to the injury, before returning last Sunday and rushing four times for 28 yards in a 40-23 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. He has rushed for 1,142 yards and eight touchdowns in 49 career games (three starts) since being selected by the Titans in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Tulane. The Tennessee Titans placed Tyjae Spears on injured reserve Saturday and elevated fellow running back Michael Carter from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the host Dallas Cowboys. Spears, 25, has rushed for 94 yards and added 16 catches for 65 yards in seven games this season. Although Tony Pollard serves as the team's workhorse running back, Carter could receive a few carries on Sunday when the Titans (1-8) face the Cowboys (4-6) in Arlington, Texas. Carter, 27, has rushed three times for seven yards in three games this season with Tennessee. away.headline: Titans' Overloaded Injury Report May Put an Upset Over Jaguars on Ice in Week 10
away.blurb: But what about Tate and four other major players missing the contest? That isn't even mentioning another questionable designation on, you guessed it, the offensive side of the ball. Robert Saleh's post-bye goal was for this team to come out swinging. On top of that laundry list, RB Tyjae Spears is once again questionable. Spears hasn't played since October 18, in the Titans' win over the Indianapolis Colts. Forgive our staff for entering tomorrow with a pessimistic mindset , but things simply aren't falling in a positive way for Tennessee. Of course, this doesn't negate the positive draft capital the team acquired at the deadline, nor does it cancel out Ward's progress. LB Cedric Gray missed Week 1 due to a concussion, and has still yet to return to the leading role he held last season. The Titans aren't 1-7 because of injuries, but setbacks like these have arguably led to the team ending up on the wrong side of the five one-score games they've lost. Titans' Overloaded Injury Report May Put an Upset Over Jaguars on Ice in Week 10 Skip to main content SI.COM Carnell Tate missing the Tennessee Titans' Week 8 matchup wasn't enough to derail the offense from their best performance of the season. Even in a loss, Tennessee posted 36 points and ground up some real momentum for the first time in weeks heading into the bye. That in itself isn't the issue, but it's hard to really land a hit when you're missing a hand. The Titans, in addition to Tate, will be without LBs Anthony Hill Jr. and Cody Barton, G Peter Skoronski, and P Tommy Townsend. The latter two were sent to the injured reserve list today. Titans are losing major players at the worst possible time This is a team coming apart at the seams at the worst time. One-instance absences - like Tate's in Week 8 - are easier to handle. But the Titans are a 1-7 squad down five starters against the best team in their division. However, it does mean that a Tennessee team down on their luck have caught another bad break. Tennessee can't catch a break this season You'll recall an 0-2 Titans team in a winnable situation on the road watching rookie RG Fernando Carmona Jr. exit vs. the New York Giants. Tennessee lost that game 12-7, and are just now trying to get Carmona back into the swing of things in practice. From that point of view, Week 10's injury report isn't all that surprising. Although, as the season winds down and certain decisions have to be made about this roster prior to an especially important draft, the added pressure from being down impactful talent works against the Titans' rebuilding process. We'll see how the undermanned team fares tomorrow, but for those hoping for a turnaround-sparking upset, you may want to splash cold water on that optimism ahead of time. A two-time Pro Bowler and one-time All-Pro, the longtime Tampa Bay defender has been especially stout against the run in 2026. The 2020 second-round pick has earned an 85.5 Pro Football Focus grade for his efforts against the run, the 13th-best run-defense mark among 100 qualified safeties. Additionally, he hasn't been too shabby against the pass, and has allowed just five receptions all season. And for his efforts in coverage, he's earned a 67.7 grade from PFF, the 24th-best pass-coverage mark among all qualified safeties. Consequently, the Buccaneers, which stand at just 3-6, would hardly be in an optimal situation playing without both Winfield and Mayfield on Sunday. In 55 career games, he's secured 20 interceptions, including a league-high nine during his All-Pro campaign in 2024. If he can come even remotely close to replicating that level of production, he'll provide a big boost to the back-end of the Lions’ defense. They're well-rested off their bye week, but they're set to face off against a strong 7-2 Detroit Lions team on the road in what could be the toughest remaining game on the schedule. The Bucs themselves are 3-6, but despite that, they remain one game back from the NFC South lead. The defense has been elite and the run game has been stout, but the passing offense has been a big problem for Tampa Bay — and it may not get much better, as quarterback Baker Mayfield is set to play this game while dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury. As always, we've rounded up our staff to lock in our picks for Sunday's game. Can the Bucs pull off the upset? Or will they fall to 3-7? Caleb Skinner, Writer: Lions 20, Bucs 17 It's getting to the point for the Bucs that they must win, or their season could be over. And things don't get easier this week as they take on the Lions. The Lions own one of the NFL's elite offenses and will test the Bucs' top-rated defense. It's unlikely they'll replicate their turnover margin as they did against the Bears, but they can most definitely slow Detroit down. While the defense won't be too much of a worry, the problems will once again come on the offensive side of the ball for Tampa Bay. The Lions' defense has stepped it up in recent weeks, and even without Aidan Hutchinson, they should be able to stymie the offense enough. I expect this one to be a low-scoring affair at Ford Field, with the Lions coming away with a close home victory to drop the Bucs to 3-7 on the year. Overall Record: 5-4 James Hill, Writer: Lions 24, Bucs 17 Baker Mayfield is once again on the mend from an injury. Yes, the Lions have injuries of their own with Aiden Hutchinson and Jack Campbell, but I don’t know if a hobbled Baker Mayfield or a healthy Jalon Daniels will be able to get the job done. Overall Record: 4-5 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Lions 27, Bucs 21 As much as I believe that the Buccaneers' defense is for real, I also believe the offense is not. Detroit, on the other hand, has one of the most dynamic offenses in the entire league. Beyond just the litany of weapons he has at his disposal, Jared Goff has been extremely effective playing against Bowles' blitz-heavy defenses over the past several years. For the Bucs to win, they'll need to get pressure with four to avoid sending extra guys to disrupt Goff in the pocket. The problem is, even if they do that and manage to generate turnovers like they have been so far this year on defense, the Bucs will need Baker Mayfield to look like a competent NFL QB on offense to win this football game. Sadly, I'm not sure if that version of Mayfield even exists anymore. Overall Record: 6-3 Logan Robinson, Founder: Lions 27, Bucs 20 Another battle for Todd Bowles against a high-scoring offense in Detroit. I’m excited to watch that, but the next thing I’m most intrigued about is the Bucs’ offensive passing attack. That has to improve, or Tampa Bay isn’t making the playoffs — It’s quite simple for me on that. Hopefully the bye week helped, but I’m very cautious about picking the Buccaneers. River Wells, Editor: Lions 24, Bucs 16 The Bucs have a few things going for them, but this is a passing league, and unfortunately, they don't have the passing offense to hang with good teams — much less an elite one like the Lions. The defense will likely hold the Detroit Lions' dynamic offense in check, but the passing offense won't be enough, and it could be even worse than usual with Mayfield's injury. I think the Bucs defense will keep them in it, but it won't be enough to win against a team that could end up winning the brutal NFC North this season. Consensus: Lions 5, Bucs 0 Once again, our staff isn't picking Tampa Bay whatsoever. Our staff unanimously picked the Bears two weeks ago, and we've unanimously picked the Lions here. It's any given Sunday in the NFL, so the Bucs are always in it. But they'll have to convince us that they can beat good teams, and so far, they simply haven't. picks.blurb: 4 Bold Predictions for Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions in Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Nebraska ends No. 14 Ohio State’s CFP hopes with upset win TRENDING College football live updates NBA Cup: The Beard drops 51 Oregon gets tricky in win Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates 4 Bold Predictions for Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions in Week 11 Andrew Hughes · Athlon Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 7:23 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tampa Bay Buccaneers come out of their bye at 3-6, and they've lost six games by seven points or fewer . A trip to Ford Field to face the 7-2 Detroit Lions is a tough place to start fixing that. The quarterback news is better than it looked earlier in the week. Head coach Todd Bowles said Friday that Baker Mayfield is trending in the right direction to start on his sprained foot, according to NBC Sports . Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's noon CT kickoff. 1. Bucky Irving outrushes Jahmyr Gibbs Gibbs leads the NFL with 1,000 rushing yards, and Bowles compared him to Barry Sanders this week. He's also running into the best run defense in the league . Tampa Bay allows 79.1 rushing yards per game, the fewest in the NFL, according to ESPN. We compared each back's average to what the other defense allows. Gibbs averages 111.1 rushing yards per game, about 32 more than the Bucs give up to entire offenses. Irving averages 91.7 per game on 4.9 yards per carry, almost exactly the 90.4 Detroit allows. On paper, Irving has the easier path. 2. Tez Johnson catches a 40-yard pass Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Tez Johnson (15) makes a catch past Chicago Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon (6) in the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Johnson has only 11 catches, but he's averaging 23.1 yards per reception with a long of 64, according to ESPN . Nobody else on the roster with more than five catches is close to that average. Detroit is playing without Aidan Hutchinson, and the Lions will have to respect Irving and the run game. One play-action shot to Johnson is the easiest way for a quarterback on a sore foot to change the game without having to move much. 3. The Bucs intercept Jared Goff twice Nov 1, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers cornerback Jacob Parrish (25) intercepts a pass intended for Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London (5) thrown by quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (not pictured) during the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Goff has thrown four interceptions all season, so this one is bold. Tampa Bay has 21 takeaways , and 16 of them are interceptions. Zyon McCollum and Alex Anzalone have four apiece, and Jacob Parrish has two. Parrish draws Amon-Ra St. Brown, and he's PFF's No. 4 cornerback . If Goff keeps feeding St. Brown against Bowles' zone looks, the Bucs will get a couple of chances to jump a route. 4. Tampa Bay wins its first one-score game Nov 1, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers placekicker Chase McLaughlin (4) celebrates with punter Riley Dixon (9) after kicking a thirty-four-yard field goal against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images The Bucs' three wins came by eight, 30 and 16 points. Every loss has been by seven or fewer, and the red zone is a big reason. Tampa Bay has scored touchdowns on 15 of its 31 trips inside the 20 and settled for field goals on 12 others. That's why this ends with Chase McLaughlin. He's made all 22 of his field-goal attempts this season, and a close game in Detroit finally breaks Tampa Bay's way on his leg. Bucs 23, Lions 21. (Photo by Steven King/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Erik Schlitt · SB Nation Mon, November 16, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After taking down the Patriots in Germany, the Detroit Lions (7-2) return home to Michigan for a Week 11 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) inside the comfy confines of Ford Field. While the Lions are making the long journey back from Munich, the Bucs are coming off their bye week. The Lions are playing tremendous football right now. They're currently on a five-game winning streak and are coming off a convincing win overseas, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions – 5.5 points . In the 2026 offseason, the Bucs saw several staple players depart Tampa Bay, including WR Mike Evans, LB LaVonte David, and CB Jamel Dean. The Bucs also saw QB Teddy Bridgewater (before his retirement) and DB Christian Izien leave for the Lions, while signing a handful of former Lions to their current roster, including LB Alex Anzalone, DE Al-Quadin Muhamed, DL A'Shawn Robinson, S Ifeatu Melifonwu, and S Miles Killebrew. After opening the season 0-4, the Bucs are 3-2 over their last five games, including wins over the Cowboys, Panthers, and Falcons, but lost their most recent game to the Chicago Bears. The Bears jumped out to an early 14-0 lead, but after the Bucs intercepted Bears QB Caleb Williams four (!) times, they climbed back into the game. Tampa Bay scored 11 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to tie the game at 24, but Williams got the Bears into field goal range, and Bears kicker Carlos Santos kicked the game-winner as time expired. With that loss, the Bucs have now lost all three games against NFC North teams this season, and the Lions will want to complete the sweep. away.headline: Which Buccaneers stepped up as injuries piled up before the bye?
away.blurb: His involvement was growing before the comparison period ended, reaching a season-high 30 defensive snaps against Carolina in Week 7. Walker's increased playing time is particularly important with Yaya Diaby dealing with a knee injury, although the available reporting does not establish that Walker's entire increase resulted from Diaby's absence. Injuries forced Tampa Bay to adjust before the bye, but the increased playing time also created opportunities to evaluate its depth. Chukwuma and Johnson showed they could contribute when starters were unavailable, while Durham, Sharp, and Walker earned bigger roles that could remain valuable in the second half of the season. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers entered their Week 10 bye having dealt with injuries at quarterback, wide receiver, offensive tackle, and across the defense. Those absences forced lineup adjustments, but they also gave other players chances to show what they could contribute when called upon to step up. According to DepthRoom's snap-count data , five Buccaneers increased their share of playing time by at least 10 percentage points when comparing Weeks 4–6 with Weeks 7–9. Some stepped in for injured starters, while others saw their roles expand as personnel usage changed. Chukwuma saw the biggest increase, rising from 0% of Tampa Bay's offensive snaps in Weeks 4–6 to 33% over the next three games. His opportunity came when Luke Goedeke missed Week 7 against Carolina with a calf injury. Chukwuma started at right tackle and helped Tampa Bay rush for 258 yards in a 43-13 victory. According to Scott Smith's official team report , it was Chukwuma's third career start, and Todd Bowles expressed confidence in his potential to become a full-time NFL starter. Johnson's snap share climbed from 43% to 62%, with Emeka Egbuka's absence opening a spot at wide receiver. Egbuka missed Weeks 7 and 8 while dealing with concussion and foot injuries. Johnson started against Carolina and played 41 offensive snaps, contributing a 19-yard third-down reception, a 14-yard rushing gain, and a 14-yard touchdown catch. His involvement continued growing after Egbuka returned, reaching 54 snaps, or 79% of the offense, against Chicago in Week 9. Durham increased his offensive snap share from 26% to 46%, becoming a more frequent part of Tampa Bay's tight end rotation. The Buccaneers had already shown a willingness to use multiple tight ends, including opening their Week 6 matchup against Pittsburgh with three on the field. Durham's increase reflects a larger role in those personnel packages, although no specific injury has been established as the reason for his additional playing time. Perhaps the Egubka injury contributed to lineups with more tight ends on the field. Sharp's playing time rose from 6% to 23%, giving the rookie more opportunities alongside Cade Otton and Durham. away.headline: Buccaneers May Need Rookie QB Jalon Daniels at the Worst Time
away.blurb: Mayfield’s availability remains the central variable. If he can return, the Buccaneers gain their veteran starter for an important NFC road test. If he cannot, Daniels’ legs, decision-making, and ability to avoid costly possessions will determine whether Tampa Bay can make its rushing attack the centerpiece of a credible upset bid. – The Lions placed linebacker Jack Campbell (neck) on injured reserve, while edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson (knee) is out for the season. Those absences could make Daniels’ scrambling ability and Tampa Bay’s ground game more consequential if the rookie starts. Buccaneers’ Keionte Scott Earns Rookie Recognition, but One Flaw Stands Out Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (leg) has an uncertain outlook for Sunday’s (Nov. 22) road game against the Detroit Lions, creating the possibility rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make another start. The Buccaneers need Mayfield’s status clarified quickly because Daniels’ mobility could change the offense’s approach in a matchup expected to hinge on controlling possession, protecting the football, and keeping Detroit’s high-powered attack off the field. Locked On Bucs host James Yarcho said Daniels took the first-team reps after Mayfield missed Wednesday’s practice. The official team preview also listed Mayfield’s lower-leg injury as a major question for the week and noted Tampa Bay promoted Easton Stick from the practice squad, underscoring the need for quarterback insurance. Daniels has started three games while Mayfield was sidelined. He has supplied a dimension the offense can use if he starts again. He has rushed 22 times for 123 yards, a 5.6-yard average, while completing 60 of 98 passes for 501 yards, three touchdowns, and five interceptions. Yarcho does not suggest Daniels is the more polished passer, but rather his ability to escape the pocket could extend drives against a Lions defense missing key front-seven pieces. That mobility matters most if it helps running back Bucky Irving sustain Tampa Bay’s preferred game script. Irving has 825 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns through nine games, and the Buccaneers have leaned on him heavily during their recent stretch. A Daniels start would put more pressure on the offense to pair designed quarterback movement, play-action and a disciplined rushing attack rather than asking the rookie to win a pass-heavy game from the pocket. – Irving remains the offensive centerpiece, but the Buccaneers have also discussed reducing his workload after he logged 111 carries over the previous five games. Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker could take on more work if Tampa Bay wants to preserve Irving while maintaining its physical identity. – Detroit running back Jahmyr Gibbs presents the defining test for the defense after reaching 1,000 rushing yards in nine games. home.headline: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury
home.blurb: "Nothing new," Lions coach Dan Campbell said after the game when asked for an update on Hutchinson. "We’ll know more when we get back to the States. But any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out." This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury Initial tests on Aidan Hutchinson’s injured knee showed the Detroit Lions star has a torn ACL, according to a report from NFL Network on Monday, Nov. 16. Hutchinson, 26, had initial tests performed in Germany, where the Lions beat the New England Patriots on Sunday, and will have more done in the United States, the report added. On Good Morning Football, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said, “my understanding, the belief is it’s a torn ACL and more for Aidan Hutchinson.” The injury to Hutchinson occurred in the first quarter of Detroit’s win over the Patriots. Hutchinson sacked quarterback Drake Maye and leapt into the air to celebrate. He fell to the ground after landing and grabbed his right knee. Hutchinson, who has six sacks this season, eventually walked off the field under his own power. He entered the blue medical tent on the sideline and remained there for a few moments before later walking to the locker room with trainers at his side. Campbell is scheduled to hold a news conference on Tuesday. If the report from NFL Network is correct and Hutchinson does have a torn ACL, D.J. Wonnum and rookie Derrick Moore would be expected to see an uptick in responsibilities. Wonnum has six sacks this season, and Moore has four over his last two games.

home.headline: Baker Mayfield gives injury update, latest rumors on Bucs QB's status vs. Lions
home.blurb: Mayfield said he practiced in a "limited fashion." The thumb injury held him out of action for three games. After Mayfield returned, he led the Buccaneers to two crucial divisional victories over the Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons — although the team didn't need him to complete a single pass in the latter contest. Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback is "trending toward" playing on Sunday against the Detroit Lions, according to NFL insider James Palmer . Mayfield suffered a foot sprain during Tampa Bay's 27-24 loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 8. He's still dealing with pain from the injury but is "pushing through it," according to Palmer. "If Mayfield does play, he's expected to wear a special orthotic and new cleats to help stabilize the foot," according to NFL insider Tom Pelissero . "He also has been dealing with the aftereffects of a dislocated right thumb suffered in Week 2 that sidelined him for three games. But he has now shed the special glove he wore for two games," added Pelissero. Mayfield told reporters that he "felt good" during a press conference on Thursday, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . "Just trying to get as much as I can in," Mayfield said about his practice. "The mental side of it. Hopefully, [I can] get more tomorrow and go from there." When asked if he felt like he could play this week, Mayfield nodded and confirmed: "I'm ready." The 31-year-old signed a three-year, $165 million contract extension this offseason, but the early production has left a lot to be desired. Mayfield opened the 2026 season with three consecutive losses before dislocating his thumb during a 23-16 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3. The Buccaneers went into their Week 10 bye with a 3-6 record, but they can still win a division title in the NFC South despite their struggles. Although they currently trail the Panthers by one game, ESPN Analytics gives the Buccaneers a 61 percent chance of winning the division this season. Mayfield has completed 60.6 percent of his passes for 922 yards with three touchdowns and four interceptions in six games.

away.blurb: Carson Beck has been downgraded to out for Sunday because of back spasms. On Friday, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Friday he was preparing to start Johnson after Beck did not practice due to a back injury. After not being listed on the injury report Wednesday, Beck was added on Thursday, as he was a limited participant in practice. The third-round pick out of Miami struggled to get much going in a 34-6 loss to the Rams, completing 11 of his 18 passing attempts for 108 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions, while also getting sacked five times.
