picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Nebraska ends No. 14 Ohio State’s CFP hopes with upset win TRENDING College football live updates NBA Cup: The Beard drops 51 Oregon gets tricky in win Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers are hurting in the pride department. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. They had won four straight before being embarrassed on national television by the Bengals, 38-18. The Eagles are no strangers to embarrassment this season, but for the first time in several weeks, the injury report isn't looking like a CVS receipt. WR DeVonta Smith practiced in full Thursday, as did RB Saquon Barkley, and edge rushers Jonathan Greenard and Jalyx Hunt. HC Mike McCarthy is in his first season coaching Pittsburgh, but has plenty of experience coaching against the Eagles from his days in Green Bay and Dallas. He is 3-5 lifetime in games at the Linc. Nick Sirianni is 5-0 after a bye week, but I'm not sure any amount of time will give his team enough of an advantage. Picks: Steelers -4.5 Passing Props (O/U) Aaron Rodgers: 211.5 passing yards, 1.5 TD (+140/-188) Joe Milton: 187.5 passing yards, 0.5 TD (-205/+152) Analysis: Milton did his best with the hand he was dealt two weeks ago against the Giants (18/34/169), considering he spent much of the afternoon running for his life. He'll get help with Smith – and very possibly Tay Wicks – returning to the lineup. He should also get a boost from a Steelers pass D ranked 30 th in the league. Rodgers has had an up-and-down season; he had a four-week run where he looked bulletproof, and followed it up with two games with subpar numbers: a blowout win over Cleveland, where they didn't need much from him, and their blowout loss to the Bengals, where they didn't get much. Picks: Milton OVER yards, Rodgers OVER yards Rushing Props (O/U) Jaylen Warren – 65.5 yards Saquon Barkley – 60.5 yards Rico Dowdle – 37.5 yards Milton – 34.5 yards Analysis: I feel a lot of the game script could be determined by which Jaylen Warren shows up. He has had five games with 93+ yards this season, and four with 50 or fewer, the most recent last week vs Cincy (7/15). Dowdle had three straight games of 40+ yards before last week's 5/26. I like Milton to make more plays with his legs, as he did vs NYG (9/64). It may be a better strategy than running Barkley between the tackles. Barkley may finally be healthy, but he can't block for himself. Picks: Barkley UNDER yards, Milton OVER yards Receiving Props (O/U) DeVonta Smith – 48.5 yards, 4.5 receptions DK Metcalf – 42.5 yards, 3.5 receptions Dallas Goedert – 30.5 yards, 3.5 receptions Germie Bernard – 29.5 yards, 3.5 receptions Warren – 22.5 yards, 2.5 receptions Pat Freiermuth – 20.5 yards, 2.5 receptions Darnell Washington 20.5 yards, 2.5 receptions Barkley – 10.5 yards, 1.5 receptions Dowdle – 9.5 yards, 1.5 receptions Analysis: One would think Smith will want to put on a show after missing 5 of the last 6 games, and a change in QB from Tanner McKee to Milton shouldn't put a wrinkle in that. Goedert has caught 4+ passes in L5. I can't explain what happened to DK Metcalf. 35 catches in nine games is far less than I expected, and I think Steelers fans would agree. Five catches on 28 targets over the last 3 weeks is shocking. Meanwhile, Bernard had a four-game run of 25 catches before being shutout last week. Warren has 3 catches in 6/9 this season, and 26+ yards in 8/9, he's Rodgers' main checkdown option. Picks: Smith OVER yards, OVER receptions; Warren OVER receptions, OVER yards Anytime Touchdown Washington +300 Freiermuth +330 Analysis: Either Steelers TE has scored in six straight. Play them both, just not in a parlay. Picks: Barkley, Milton, Washington, Freiermuth

Best Steelers Prop Bet vs. Bengals in NFL Week 10 Jaylen Warren OVER 64.5 Rushing Yards (-113) Steelers running back Jaylen Warren is having a monster 2026 season, averaging 5.9 yards per carry while posting four 100-yard games. He’s also cleared 64.5 rushing yards in five of his last six appearances. After entering the season in a timeshare with Rico Dowdle, Warren appears to have taken control of the lead role, playing 72.4 percent of the Steelers’ snaps. away.headline: Will Eagles RB Saquon Barkley play in Week 11 vs. Steelers? What fans should know
away.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles have dealt with plenty of injuries ahead of their Week 11 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers — including when it pertains to running back Saquon Barkley, who has been hampered by a few key health setbacks in 2026. I did that the past two weeks. After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow. The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14 Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well. Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13 Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Carolina Panthers Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close. Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22 New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers (-3.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17 Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (-3) In Mexico, Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders (+6.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. Pick: Bengals 34, Commanders 30 Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. away.headline: NFL fans react to Ravens’ rumored plan for Lamar Jackson’s return after thumb injury
away.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens believe Lamar Jackson has a chance to return from his broken right thumb for their Week 16 game against the Cleveland Browns on Dec. 27 if his rehab goes smoothly, ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported this week. Lamar Jackson’s Road From Buffalo Toward a Possible Browns Return In a statement the team released that day, head coach Jesse Minter called recovery timelines “challenging to predict” and said, “He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.” Minter added, “We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season.” Graziano’s report hinges on Jackson’s progress in the same way, leaving the Browns game at M&T Bank Stadium a possibility rather than a set date for his return. For another fan, the calendar is the problem, since a return against the Browns would leave Jackson only two more regular-season games after that one. A Dec. 27 return would be near the optimistic end of Jackson’s reported recovery timetable, though the Ravens have emphasized that his progress, rather than a fixed date, will determine when he can play again. The report comes with Baltimore at 4-6, days after a 23-20 home loss to the Los Angeles Chargers, who had not won a game before Monday night. Despite the prospect of Jackson returning for the final stretch of the regular season, several fans who responded to the report argued that the Ravens should keep him sidelined and focus on having him healthy for 2027. Jackson’s injury came on Baltimore’s first offensive play of the Nov. 1 game at Buffalo, a 36-10 loss, when his throwing hand caught the arm of Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau as he threw. On Nov. 13, the Ravens said the thumb was dislocated and broken and that the injury typically carries a recovery of six to 10 weeks. Sources told ESPN’s Adam Schefter that Jackson had undergone surgery the week before. Fans Point to the Baltimore Ravens’ Slide and Jackson’s Long-Term Health “Week 16 is so late. Just shut him down and run it back next year,” the fan wrote. Baltimore’s form has added to the argument. The Ravens sit fourth in the AFC North and have lost five straight games, including the Buffalo game in which Jackson was hurt and both games since. Jacoby Brissett, whom Baltimore acquired in a trade, started in Jackson’s place in the loss to the Chargers. “It’s already over … just take the rest of the season off,” another fan responded. Jackson’s health is another piece of it. A high ankle sprain had already cost him three games before the thumb injury, and he has played just 14 full quarters this season. A fan pointed to that history: “Yea bro let’s have Lamar play meaningless games in a lost season after 2 major injuries.” Others looked straight ahead to next season. “What’s the point to play him at that point, come back ’27 stronger,” one fan wrote. The Jets got the ball to start the third quarter. Cade Klubnik took over for an injured Geno Smith and made a few nice plays with his leg and his arm to get the Jets in scoring position. They settled for a field goal to get within a point of the Bills at 10 – 9 early in the third quarter. That was as close as the Jets would get in the game. picks.headline: Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: Los Angeles Chargers
picks.blurb: Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: Los Angeles Chargers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Nebraska ends No. 14 Ohio State’s CFP hopes with upset win TRENDING College football live updates NBA Cup: The Beard drops 51 Oregon gets tricky in win Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates Previewing the New York Jets’ opposition: Los Angeles Chargers EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 06: (NEW YORK DAILIES OUT) Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers in action against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on November 06, 2023 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Chargers defeated the Jets 27-6. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bent Double · SB Nation Sat, November 21, 2026 at 3:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The last time the Jets beat the Chargers, they were still representing San Diego and Plaxico Burress scored three touchdowns. Since that time, New York have lost five straight times to them, including a 27-6 drubbing in their most recent meeting in 2023. Let's break down the Chargers' roster going position by position: Justin Herbert was a pro bowler last season, but he's having a rough year in 2026, with career-worst numbers in almost every category. In his first six seasons, he averaged 27 touchdown passes and 11 interceptions per year. However, over halfway through the 2026 season, he has thrown for just six touchdown passes and already has 11 interceptions. He didn't have a very productive game as a passer against the Ravens on Monday night, but at least he managed not to throw an interception for the first time all year as the Chargers finally won their first game to improve to 1-8. He also rushed for a season-high 51 yards and a touchdown. DJ Uiagalelei is the backup but he's completed just two NFL passes in his career. Offensive Line Incredibly, five of the Chargers' eight active offensive linemen are rookies, although this is hardly by design. They have five offensive linemen on injured reserve, including well known names like Rashawn Slater, Tyler Biadasz, Trevor Penning and Trey Pipkins. Pipkins was activated for practice last week, though, so his return is possible on Sunday. His official game status is questionable. Unsurprisingly, this has led to the Chargers struggling to protect Herbert, who has been sacked 33 times. Only Deshaun Watson has been sacked more often that that this season. The only two players to start every game so far have been second round rookie Jake Slaughter at center and veteran right guard Cole Strange. At the moment, Joe Alt is at left tackle, with sixth round rookie Logan Taylor at left guard. Slater and Penning had started off the year on the left side, but Alt moved across from right tackle and Taylor stepped in when each of them got hurt. Since Alt's move, fourth round rookie Travis Burke has been starting at right tackle. Alt has a team-high seven penalties and Strange, who has also given up a team-high three sacks, has six. The three players currently on the bench are veteran guard Kayode Awosika, sixth round tackle Alex Harkey and the undrafted center Jacob Spomer. Awosika and Harkey have started two games each this season. Running Backs Los Angeles' top running back, Omarion Hampton, last season's number one pick, is still averaging less than four yards per carry behind the banged-up line, although the Chargers rank 10th in the NFL for rushing offense. He's coming off his first 100-yard rushing performance of the season in the win over the Ravens. Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal both get work as backups to Hampton but they combined for just four yards on five carries in the Ravens win. They have caught 30 passes and scored three touchdowns between them, though. Scott Matlock is also on the roster as a fullback with Alec Ingold on injured reserve. Pass catchers The leading receiver so far this year for the Chargers is last year's second round pick Tre Harris who has 26 catches for 348 yards but no touchdowns. You would have expected Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnson to produce more alongside Harris but they've only started eight games between them and combined for just 31 catches. However, they've flashed big play potential with Johnson averaging 19 yards per catch and McConkey averaging 17. On Monday, McConkey – who is questionable for Sunday – was inactive and Harris was the only Charger with more than 16 receiving yards. At tight end, Oronde Gadsen II has caught 20 passes and Charlie Kolar has caught 15, but David Njoku has been a non-factor. Njoku could play more this week, though, because Kolar has been dealing with a concussion and is listed as questionable. The backups at wide receiver are Theo Wease Jr., KeAndre Lambert-Smith, Derius Davis and fourth round rookie Brenen Thompson. They've combined for 12 catches, half of which were by Lambert-Smith. Thompson is listed as doubtful for Sunday. Defensive Line The Chargers operate with a 3-4 system that employs Jamaree Caldwell, Dalvin Tomlinson and Teair Tart as starters. They are poor against the pass, but middle of the pack against the run, and held the Ravens to 16 yards on 15 carries on Monday night. Fifth round rookie Nick Barrett and Justin Eboigbe are the backups inside. All five have played at least 140 snaps with Tomlinson having contributed 2.5 sacks. The Chargers drafted Akheem Mesidor in the first round but he's currently coming off the bench behind veteran Khalil Mack and 2025 pro bowler Tuli Tuipolotu. While none of the three has more than three sacks, they've combined for 8.5. Mack leads the team with six tackles for loss, while Tuipolotu leads them with 16 quarterback hits. At inside linebacker, Daiyan Henley plays a full-time role and wears the headset. He leads the team with 62 tackles but has been bothered by a knee issue all year, which even nixed a potential trade to Denver. The knee issue has ruled him out for Sunday. The other starter has been former Jet Del'Shawn Phillips, although Henley was sometimes the only off-ball linebacker on the field. Backups Troy Dye and Marlowe Wax don't get to play much but Wax should have a bigger role with Henley out. Bud Dupree and Caleb Murphy are the backups on the outside but neither has played much. Defensive Backs Aside from all their injuries on the offensive line, the Chargers have also been deeply impacted by pro bowl safety Derwin James being on injured reserve. Tony Jefferson and Elijah Molden are the current starters at safety, although RJ Mickens and fourth round rookie Genesis Smith have also played over 200 snaps each. Kendall Williamson is also on the roster but hasn't played on defense and has been listed as out anyway. Tarheeb Still and Donte Jackson are the starting cornerbacks with Still reverting to the slot in nickel packages and Cam Hart entering the game on the outside. Hart has two interceptions and a team-high eight pass breakups. Still practiced all week but showed up on the injury report on Friday and is listed as questionable. Backups Rodney Shelley, Isas Waxter and Deane Leonard have all played less than 100 snaps at cornerback. Shelley is another undrafted rookie but he's been ruled out, while Waxter is also listed as questionable. Special Teams The Chargers' kicking game is pretty solid with kicker Cameron Dicker having only missed two kicks all season. He also has the third-lowest opponents' kickoff return average in the NFL. While punter JK Scott's raw numbers are not eye-popping, Pro Football Focus currently ranks him first in the league based on their grades. Davis, Mitchell and Vidal have all seen work on kickoff returns, with nobody managing a 35-yard return so far this year. The Jets should be wary of Davis, though, as he had an 87-yard punt return for a touchdown against them in 2023. He's averaging 10 yards per return on punts with Thompson and McConkey listed as his backups. Jets fans may recall what a good special teams contributor Phillips was, and he's continued in that vein by leading the Chargers in special teams tackles again despite moving into the starting unit. He led the entire NFL last year. Wax, Murphy and Dye are also productive, while the primary gunners have been Lambert-Smith and the backup cornerbacks.

picks.blurb: Chargers Unanimously Picked By ESPN Experts to Defeat Jets in Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Nebraska ends No. 14 Ohio State’s CFP hopes with upset win TRENDING College football live updates NBA Cup: The Beard drops 51 Oregon gets tricky in win Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates Chargers Unanimously Picked By ESPN Experts to Defeat Jets in Week 11 (James Lang-Imagn Images) Aiden Checketts · Roundtable Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 7:20 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Chargers finally got in the win column as they picked up their first win of the season, defeating the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 on the road on Monday Night Football. After winning their first game of the 2026 season, it is going to be interesting to see how LA approaches the rest of the season , and whether they are competitive or end up with a top draft pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That said, the focus now moves to their home matchup this week against the New York Jets in a game that could have a lot to do with how the draft order pans out. On that note, ESPN put out a Week 11 preview done by NFL Nation as well as fantasy football writer Eric Moody, analytics writer Seth Walder, and sports betting analyst Pamela Maldonado, who picked each game, and when it came to the Chargers and Jets matchup, LA was the unanimous pick. Now, in terms of the picks, Maldonado had the Chargers winning 24-20, Moody had a 23-17 victory for LA, and Walder picked Los Angeles to 23-20. All that to say, it is very clear that this ESPN panel does like the Chargers this week, and despite the fact the season has been rough for LA thus far, sometimes after picking up a win, a team can get into a rhythm and start stacking wins. One thing to note on the Chargers side, is the fact that they did a great job on the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball on Monday night against the Ravens. Starting with the defense, LA held running back Derrick Henry to 10 yards rushing on 10 carries and the Ravens 15 attempts for 16 yards as a team. That is a great performance for LA and because of that, it forced quarterback Jacoby Brissett to put the the game on his shoulders and the Chargers were able to do just enough to get the win through picking him off once and recovering a fumble from wide receiver Zay Flowers. Now on the offensive side, the Chargers ran the ball very well with running back Omarion Hampton tallying 22 carries for 105 yards and one score in addition to quarterback Justin Herbert adding seven carries for 51 yards and a touchdown. As a team, LA ran the ball 34 times for 160 yards while averaging 4.7 yards per carry. All that to say, the formula for the Chargers in Week 10 was dominating on both sides of the line of scrimmage which worked out and enabled them to pick up a win which was huge for their confidence, but also shows that they do not need to lean on Herbert. away.headline: New York Jets rookie Cade Klubnik suddenly thrust into NFL debut after Geno Smith suffers brief injury against Bills
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The New York Jets lost quarterback Geno Smith to an injury in their Week 10 game against the Buffalo Bills, and rookie Cade Klubnik came in to the offense in a division showdown. Smith took a hit late in the first half and did not return for the start of the second half. For a Jets team that needed a clean afternoon against Buffalo, this likely won't help. Smith went to the blue medical tent after the play. When the second half kicked off, he was nowhere to be seen, and Klubnik jogged out with the offense instead. Klubnik is the only other active quarterback on the Jets roster. That means there is no veteran waiting on the sideline and no safety net if things go sideways. New York drafted him in the fourth round out of Clemson, and his first NFL snaps are coming against Buffalo with a division game on the line. Will Levis is currently on the practice squad . New York’s divisional showdown took an unexpected turn when its starting quarterback left the game, forcing a promising rookie into a difficult NFL debut. Smith has now returned to play. Smith has now cleared concussion protocol and is back into the game against Buffalo. How Geno Smith got hurt against the Bills The Jets were driving in the final two minutes of the first half and had worked their way into the red zone. On third down, Smith pulled the ball down and scrambled before throwing the ball away at the last second. Bills linebacker Terrel Bernard caught him and delivered a hit to the rib area. The New York Jets have a 9% chance at the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft and a 78% chance at a top-5 pick, according to the A to Z Sports NFL Playoff Predictor (updated Sun, Nov 15). Geno Smith’s injury was being evaluated for a concussion. Smith has now passed the concussion protocol . That detail matters. The hit landed on his ribs, but a concussion evaluation is a different situation entirely and comes with its own protocol. Cade Klubnik gets thrown into the fire for a drive Klubnik was able to use his legs to help the Jets drive down the field and get another field goal on the board. Of course, the Jets got down near the red zone and weren’t able to convert for 7. That has been the theme of the season and of today so far. Geno Smith has returned to the game and looks to be able to finish it the rest of the way, barring another injury. As much as I would like to see Klubnik get some opportunity, this is definitely the best situation for New York if they want to have a chance to win this one. Smith has had a very solid season so far and has been able to move the football today. The Jets just haven’t been able to get it into the end zone. Against a team like Buffalo, they’ll need to change that in the second half. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.headline: Report: Raiders TE Brock Bowers avoids major ankle injury
away.blurb: The team initially listed him as questionable to return and he came back in the second quarter with his right ankle heavily taped. He made one catch before returning to the locker room and ultimately being ruled out. Bowers, 23, finished the 21-13 defeat with two receptions for 18 yards. The third-year pro out of Georgia raised his team-leading season totals to 50 catches for 676 yards with six touchdowns. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Bowers is day-to-day. "It's not as bad as we thought but still a significant injury, so we'll keep monitoring him," Kubiak said. Bowers, a two-time Pro Bowl selection, was hurt while blocking on a running play during the Raiders' opening drive. Multiple players rolled up on the back of his leg as he was making the block. A first-round pick (13th overall) by Las Vegas in 2024, Bowers has accumulated 226 receptions for 2,550 yards and 18 touchdowns in 37 career games (32 starts). He was a first-team All-Pro as a rookie. This story was originally published November 16, 2026 at 10:59 AM . After missing the last four games with an ankle injury, safety Talanoa Hufanga will make his return after being a full participant in practice all week long. Brandon Jones , however, is listed as questionable for Sunday's game after being a limited participant in practice all week long with a hamstring injury that he re-aggravated during Denver's game against the Kansas City Chiefs. They do have a spot open on the 53-man roster right now, and veteran safety Taylor Rapp could be a candidate to secure that spot, considering he's out of practice squad elevations. Jahdae Barron also played some safety against the Panthers and could be an option if Jones can't go. Tight end Caleb Lohner's 21-day window opened this week in practice, and there is no rush for Denver to necessarily bring him onto the active roster right away, which leaves his official status as out for Sunday's game by default. away.headline: Raiders dealt considerable injury disadvantage with Broncos coming off their bye
away.blurb: After a physical game against the Seattle Seahawks last Sunday, the Raiders are dealing with a few bumps and bruises; nothing out of the ordinary. But the Broncos are coming off their bye, so they practically have a clean bill of health heading into this heated divisional matchup. Concussions can often keep a player out for one game, but because Denver had its bye week, both players were able to make a full recovery. And that's a good thing, because head and neck health is important, but it certainly does not help Las Vegas' chances of winning in Week 11. Matt Gay being a bit banged up is not great, either. He has been lights-out as a kicker this year, and with the ball moving differently at a mile above sea level on Sunday, Las Vegas needs him to be at the top of his game. Hip injuries can be worrisome for a kicker, depending on the hip, of course. With the Broncos not having any injury concerns this week, fresh off their bye, it hurts to have Bowers potentially out and another starter at least banged up. But the Raiders haven't done well playing against injured teams this year, so maybe they'll thrive with the shoe on the other foot. But one benefit that they've carried in their back pocket throughout the campaign has been relatively good health , which has given them an edge in seemingly every single game. Have the Silver and Black always taken advantage of that edge? No. But in several contests, they have gotten to face skeleton crews with a fully staffed roster. away.blurb: Unfortunately, that coincides with the Raiders now dealing with a few key ailments in what feels like a must-win matchup to keep their playoff hopes alive and to finally earn a signature win. Tonka Hemingway ruled out for Las Vegas' game vs. Denver Hemingway did not leave the Week 10 game against the Seahawks at any point, but he noticeably grimaced when leaving the field a handful of times. After not participating in any of the three practices this week, Hemingway was ruled out on Friday, so he will not be in uniform against Denver. Kubiak told the media that they needed to "keep evaluating" Hemingway, but perhaps he just didn't want the Broncos to have a head start on getting that info. With Hemingway out, the Raiders will have to rely on some combination of Tim Keenan III, JJ Pegues and Thomas Booker IV to step up in his place. home.headline: Raiders dealt considerable injury disadvantage with Broncos coming off their bye
home.blurb: After a physical game against the Seattle Seahawks last Sunday, the Raiders are dealing with a few bumps and bruises; nothing out of the ordinary. But the Broncos are coming off their bye, so they practically have a clean bill of health heading into this heated divisional matchup. Concussions can often keep a player out for one game, but because Denver had its bye week, both players were able to make a full recovery. And that's a good thing, because head and neck health is important, but it certainly does not help Las Vegas' chances of winning in Week 11. Matt Gay being a bit banged up is not great, either. He has been lights-out as a kicker this year, and with the ball moving differently at a mile above sea level on Sunday, Las Vegas needs him to be at the top of his game. Hip injuries can be worrisome for a kicker, depending on the hip, of course. With the Broncos not having any injury concerns this week, fresh off their bye, it hurts to have Bowers potentially out and another starter at least banged up. But the Raiders haven't done well playing against injured teams this year, so maybe they'll thrive with the shoe on the other foot. Not even close to everything has gone right for the Las Vegas Raiders during the 2026 NFL season. But one benefit that they've carried in their back pocket throughout the campaign has been relatively good health , which has given them an edge in seemingly every single game. Have the Silver and Black always taken advantage of that edge? No. But in several contests, they have gotten to face skeleton crews with a fully staffed roster. That is changing this week, though, with the AFC West rival Denver Broncos on the schedule for Week 11. All year, Las Vegas has been at an advantage in the injury department. For the 7-2 Jaguars, they are fighting to secure the AFC South for the second year in a row, as well as fighting for a top seed in a tight AFC playoff race. To beat the Giants, who have exceeded expectations in their first year under John Harbaugh, the Jaguars will need to be at their best. So, how do we see the Jaguars' big test against the Giants playing out? We break it down with this week's bold predictions. Bhayshul Tuten Hits 100 Yards Rushing No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues. According to NextGenStats, "Tuten has forced a missed tackle on 33.3% of his carries this season, the third-highest rate among running backs with at least 100 carries, behind only Kenneth Walker III (38.0%) and Jahmyr Gibbs (36.7%). He has forced 49 missed tackles on the ground, the fourth-most in the NFL, with 267 of his 609 rushing yards coming after forcing missed tackles (43.8%), the highest share among that same group of backs. Giants' defenders have missed 15.0% of their tackle opportunities this season, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the Broncos (17.5%)." Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. The Jaguars' entire offensive identity is being balanced, and running Tuten in heavier packages could be the only way for the Jaguars to get the Giants out of their blitz looks. Jaguars Limit Giants to Under 3.5 YPC The Giants have had something going with their running game lately, with Giants running back/mascot Cam Skattebo turning in his two best games of the season over his last two performances. In Weeks 7 and 10 combined, Skattebo rushed 35 times for 202 yards (5.77 yards per carry) for three touchdowns. He has a limited skill-set, but he has been able to pave the way for the Giants running game. With that in mind, I think we see the Jaguars get back to their elite run defense this week after back-to-back weeks allowing too many chunk yards. I think the difference in talent level between Jordan Davis and the rest of the Jaguars' nose tackle options is significant enough that the addition of Davis to the defensive line this week should make all of the difference. The run defense has not been the same without Davon Hamilton, but now the Jaguars finally have their reinforcement set to debut. Parker Washington Makes Another 50+ Yard Catch No receiver has made bigger plays for the Jaguars this year than Parker Washington, who has been the Jaguars' primary downfield receiver all season. He has caught a 50-yard pass in back-to-back weeks, first for a touchdown in Week 9 and then last week to set up a scoring drive against the Titans. With the way the Giants like to play defense with their cornerbacks, I believe this week could be prime for another big Washington grab. According to NextGen Stats, "Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4) among receivers with at least 25 routes against press coverage. Washington has faced press on a team-high 46 routes, drawing 16 targets on those plays (34.8%), the eighth-highest target rate among that same group. He has turned those targets into 229 yards (7th-most) and three touchdowns (T-5th-most), while recording 100 receiving yards over expected, the second-most, trailing only Smith-Njigba (+179). The Giants' defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL.." The Giants are going to want to play press-man coverage and challenge the Jaguars receivers at the line of scrimmage. This is where Washington has thrived, and where Trevor Lawrence has trusted him time and time again. I expect another day full of big plays from the Jaguars' No. 1 wide receiver. Jaguars Force 3 J.J. McCarthy Turnovers J.J. McCarthy has not been the turnover prone quarterback that he was in Minnesota in his few games with the Giants, throwing two interceptions over the last month. With that in mind, I think this is the week the Jaguars can let the takeaways flow due to the nature of how McCarthy plays. McCarthy is at his best when he is extending plays with his legs and creating outside of the pocket, but the Jaguars' defense as a whole is meant to counter that. The Jaguars' entire defensive scheme is about forcing the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly, and these are the scenarios where McCarthy's issues with accuracy and decision-making show up the most. I see the Jaguars getting two interceptions and a forced fumble on McCarthy, largely because the Jaguars' style of defense will let McCarthy play right into their hands. He is playing OK, which is far better than what he showed in Minnesota, but I think the Jaguars get after him this week. Jessie Bates III Plays Every Snap Jessie Bates III did not make his Jaguars debut in Week 10 as they opted to give him the bye week he never got in Atlanta this season, which means Sunday vs. the Giants will be the first time we see the All-Pro safety in Jaguars threads. While the Jaguars took their time with letting Bates and Davis hit the field on game day, I believe their let them play big roles this week. Due to the nature of the position, I believe that means Bates will play every single snap at safety next to Antonio Johnson. The Jaguars have gotten by the last few weeks with Rayuan Lane as their No. 2 safety option, but last week's game against the Titans made it clear that he is better as depth and as a role player. There is no reason for the Jaguars to not let Bates play the entire game this week, which will mark 13 days since he was traded for. picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Nebraska ends No. 14 Ohio State’s CFP hopes with upset win TRENDING College football live updates NBA Cup: The Beard drops 51 Oregon gets tricky in win Colts cut Daniel Jones More NFL live updates NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants face major test this week when they face the Jacksonville Jaguars. It is also a game that will provide a huge swing in the Giants' expected chances to make the playoffs. Will the Giants upset Jacksonville? See what our Big Blue View staff members think about that game and the rest of the Week 11 action in this week's staff picks. I don't think the Giants win this game. I think there's a path to a win for the Giants, if they can find it. The Giants are one of the very best teams in the NFL at forcing drives to end in punts. At the same time, the Jaguars will be without their starting center and the Giants are one of the best teams in the League at creating quick pressure. That's important because Trevor Lawrence has been one of the quarterbacks most affected by pressure in the NFL. At the same time, the Giants have rediscovered the explosive pass with J.J. McCarthy, which has been the weakness of the Jags' defense. If the Giants can score touchdowns while disrupting Lawrence, they've got the chance to come away with the upset. We've seen the Giants rebound after bad games, as well as play much better than anticipated when they're underdogs. Maybe both will happen here. The flip side of the coin is simpler and scarier to me: The Giants have one of the worst red zone defenses in the NFL, and the Jaguars have one of the best red zone offenses in the league. If the Giants can't stop them between the 20s, this game could get ugly fast. Pick: Jaguars Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the league with a young and explosive offense that can run the football. Their defense is aggressive but doesn't NEED to bring the blitz — they blitz at about a league-average rate, but Anthony Campanile does an excellent job utilizing simulated pressure to harass opposing quarterbacks. Jacksonville is third in offensive EPA, 4th in defensive EPA allowed, and 1st in Net EPA — they're a juggernaut based on their performance and the advanced analytics. Still, that doesn't mean the Giants don't have a chance — they just must play efficient football and avoid the catastrophic mistakes that have robbed them of wins. It's possible, but against the most efficient team in the NFL, it will be difficult. John Harbaugh will have the Giants ready and prepared for the game, and I believe it will be more exciting and competitive. Jacksonville is concluding their third straight road game, which could give the Giants a slight advantage at home, but I ultimately believe the better team finds a way to win. David Hartman It took 11 weeks, but for the first time this season, the Giants will face a team with a winning record when the 7-2 Jaguars come to town on Sunday. Not only is Jacksonville running away with the AFC South (they lead the division by four games), but they're steamrolling the competition. They've won their last three games by a combined 75 points. This is easily Big Blue's toughest test of the season, so far. Jacksonville is very good on both sides of the ball. They're fourth in offensive DVOA, third in defensive DVOA, and third in overall DVOA. They also have an excellent field goal kicker with crazy range. If you look at both rosters, it's hard to find clear advantages for the Giants at any position group outside of tight end, and even there, Jacksonville has good players. Can the Giants win this game? Yes. They're at home, they're getting an extra three days of rest, and as we saw when they played Houston, they aren't scared and can surprise as a big underdog. They'll need to dial it up on defense and pressure Trevor Lawrence into the kinds of mistakes he used to make before Liam Coen got there. They also might have a little extra motivation after letting last week's game against the Commanders slip away at the end. I won't be surprised if John Harbaugh's team hangs in there and keeps it as a one-score game most of the way. But in the end, until the Giants show me that they can beat a really good team, I can't pick them to do so. Tony Del Genio You can talk yourself into believing that the Giants can beat Jacksonville this Sunday. They needed a miraculous last-second 57-yard field goal to beat the Eagles team (with Jalen Hurts) that the Giants defeated (without Hurts). They lost to the Texans team that the Giants beat the following week. The woeful Titans were within a TD against them last week with 5 minutes left. So indeed, it could be a competitive game. Unfortunately, the Jags have also won games by 24, 29, 35, and 23 points this season. They have scored 31 or more in each of their past four games, and over 40 in two of those. The Giants have only scored more than 30 points once, and only then because of a 99-yard pick-6 on the last play of the game. Trevor Lawrence isn't necessarily playing any better this year than in the past. He's a QB that simultaneously makes great passes and puts the ball up for grabs, yet unlike in years past, he's cut down on the INTs while getting the TDs. Part of that may be due to 5'10" wide receiver Parker Washington (a 2023 6th-round pick), who had a breakout 2025 and is on pace for 1,000 yards. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, a 4th round 2025 pick, isn't quite in the Jahmyr Gibbs – Kenneth Walker class but he's not far below and is a missed tackle machine. A lot of the credit has to go to head coach Liam Coen, who also calls the plays and turned this team around as soon as he was hired. Lawrence, like most QBs, has trouble with pressure, but he is not too fazed by the blitz. Finding a way to disrupt his rhythm is a key to any chance the Giants may have. On defense, the Jaguars are strong at linebacker with fourth-round 2023 pick Ventrell Miller, one of the league's best (note how many mid-round picks the Jags have hit on), along with Foyesade Oluokun. They also put on a decent pass rush with Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, and Dennis Gardeck. In the secondary, Travis Hunter is playing more like a No. 2 pick, having mostly given up his evening gig as a receiver. Are the Giants a serious playoff contender? This is the type of game they can use to make a statement against a team that is in the Super Bowl conversation. I think they'll put up a fight. I also don't think they're there yet. Pick : Jaguars Valentine's View I want to convince myself to pick the Giants to defeat the Jaguars. I really do. I just can't. The Jaguars are a team with justifiable Super Bowl ambitions . They are a well-rounded team with a high-powered offense, a very good defense, and one of the best field-goal kickers in the business in Cam Little. The Giants are a good team. They are resilient. They will give the Jaguars their best shot. Maybe, just maybe, it will be good enough to pull off an upset that would go a long way toward ensuring that the Giants make the playoffs. I just can't pick them to do it.

Giants game Paul Bretl, Jaguars Wire · Jaguars Wire Sat, November 21, 2026 at 1:11 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Up next for the Jacksonville Jaguars is another road matchup, this time against the New York Giants . The Jaguars will enter this game at 7-2, while the Giants are 5-3-1. The last time these two met was in 2022 , and a lot has changed for both teams since then. So for some insight into this current Giants team, Dan Benton of Giants Wire answered a handful of our questions about Sunday's game. How has the addition of JJ McCarthy impacted the Giants' offense? Giants Wire: McCarthy's presence has actually had a significant impact. Matt Nagy had designed the Giants' offense specifically around Jaxson Dart's abilities and when he was lost for the season, they were forced to trim their playbook by up to 50 percent to accommodate Jameis Winston. With McCarthy under center, Nagy was able to restore that 50 percent and run the offense the way he designed it initially. What is the strength of this Giants team this season? Giants Wire: It has been their secondary, without question. Although they have a rotation at safety, the cornerbacks have been able to win one-on-one matchups with impressive frequency. Deonte Banks has gone from an all-time Giants bust into their CB1, and deservedly so. Greg Newsome, who Jaguars fans know all too well, has also played much better than anticipated, earning a contract extension. On the flip side, where have they struggled? Giants Wire: The interior offensive line has been especially poor when it comes to run blocking. They're easily beaten — often embarrassingly so — and it has stymied the running game that was built on power and inside runs. Defensively, while they generate considerable pressure, they've been unable to close and their sack numbers are way down. Then there's the obvious: Rookie kicker Dominic Zvada's struggles from the right hash (hasn't made a single field goal from said hash). Who is an under-the-radar player to know? Giants Wire: Normally, I would have said Banks, but I feel like he's earned his way back onto everyone's radar. Rookie wide receiver Malachi Fields is beginning to emerge and has all but secured the WR2 role, and has become McCarthy's clutch third option behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely, who is having a career season. Fields has yet to drop a pass this season and both his target share and production have steadily increased. Prediction: Who wins and why? Giants Wire: I am predicting an upset. Call it lifelong recognition that the Giants will sometimes play either up or down to the level of the competition. They played down to the competition and lost in Week 10, and will play up to the competition on Sunday in the rain at MetLife Stadium, balancing things back out with a game against the Colts looming. There's no rhyme or reason that this happens, but it's what I'll call an odd Giants tradition. Giants 31, Jaguars 30. away.headline: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus
away.blurb: The Jaguars had 11 players carry either a limited or did-not-participate designation into Thursday's practice. Some names, like center Robert Hainsey's DNP situation due to a knee injury, were expected. But there was one change to Thursday's injury report that will trump all other names: Bhayshul Tuten, who was downgraded to a non-participant in practice after practicing in a limited fashion on Wednesday, which now creates quite the injury development to monitor before the Jaguars play the New York Giants in Week 11 on Sunday afternoon. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen has said in recent days that he has been pleased with Tuten's performances and toughness over the last two weeks. Add this to the fact that he played the last few weeks without a full week of practice, and it is hard to imagine Tuten sitting this one out, even if his injury will now come even more into focus. The Jaguars also had the following players listed as limited on Thursday: Jaguars-Giants Injury Report: Bhayshul Tuten's Status Once Again Takes Top Focus Skip to main content SI.COM JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- We are at that point of the season where injury reports closer resemble CVS receipts, and the Jaguars' Thursday injury report certainly checks that box. Tuten's status is a key one to watch any week, but especially in Week 11 when the Jaguars' running game is supposed to be pivotal against a blitz-happy Giants front that will test the Jaguars in the trenches. Tuten has played in each of the last two games despite practicing just once in those two weeks, and the Jaguars clearly did not feel like Tuten couldn't handle the bulk of the carries when he got 26 carries against the Titans on Sunday. “Obviously, last year being in a supplemental role, and I thought he was tough last year in some of the runs that he had where he just would kind of get whacked pretty good, get up and continue to play," Coen said on Wednesday. "To carry the load that he took this past week with 26 carries and play the amount of snaps he played still not quite 100%. I think the guy is probably mentally and physically tougher than I would've maybe imagined in ways." The smart bet would be to prepare for Tuten to play, but that does not mean this will not be a situation to monitor. It is such a key injury to watch in large part because the Jaguars have leaned on Tuten significantly over the course of the season. The second-year running back is arguably one of the three most important players on the offense alongside Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington, and he has vastly outproduced the rest of the Jaguars' running back room. This is a big one, just like each game is a big one. But unless something changes on Friday, Tuten still should be considered a key part of Sunday's game. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. The Bengals are 6-2 SU and 6-1-1 ATS in their last eight road games and have scored at least 30 points in three straight on the road. picks.headline: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Before Week 11 SNF vs. 49ers in Mexico City
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Before Week 11 SNF vs. 49ers in Mexico City Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Even if you’re not a fan of the Vikings or 49ers, Sunday night’s primetime match in Mexico City is the definition of a “must-watch.” Two of the best teams in the NFL colliding on the international stage, with playoff seeding and bragging rights on the line, is everything the NFL dreamed of when it set the 2026 schedule last spring. The stakes could not be much higher for a late-November game, and I expect both teams to put on a show. With a newfound Kirk Cousins-sized confidence boost in Minnesota , the Vikings should be set up well to meet the moment. Here are three things I see happening Sunday night at Estadio Banorte. 1. Vikings' defense slows down 49ers' attack The 49ers have been one of the most balanced offenses in the NFL, averaging a league-high 399.8 yards per game. They’re averaging the seventh-most passing yards per game at 255.8 and the third-most rushing yards per game at 144. San Francisco is also second in the league with 31.2 points per game. Simply put, the 49ers' offense can move the ball any way it needs to. The Minnesota Vikings defense ranks 1st in dropback success rate allowed, per @SumerSports The San Francisco 49ers offense ranks 1st in dropback success rate and has the highest dropback success rate of any team through 10 weeks since the 2018 Saints The Vikings' defense, on the other hand, has allowed the fewest points (14) and the second-fewest yards (236.1) per game to opposing offenses. They’ve also held their own against some of the league's best offenses, holding Detroit, Buffalo, and Green Bay to 19, 23, and 10 points over the last few weeks. Now that they have a dependable QB to keep the offense on the field, they’ll be able to catch their breath in the high altitude of Mexico City. Minnesota's defense will need all hands on deck to slow down an elite offense, but Brian Flores will certainly have his unit ready. Give me the Vikings defense to hold the 49ers under 330 total yards and 24 points. 2. Jauan Jennings finds the end zone The Vikings signed Jauan Jennings this past May for two main reasons: to open up the run game as a blocker and to be a reliable third wide receiver after Jalen Nailor’s departure in free agency. So far, neither has materialized the way head coach Kevin O’Connell and interim general manager Rob Brzezinski had hoped. Jennings has also missed the Vikings’ past two games with a calf injury, after previously missing Week 2 to attend to a personal family matter. Now, with Jennings set to return against his former team and WR2 Jordan Addison missing time, the former 49er has his chance to shine . Jennings’s struggles this season have largely been due to poor quarterbacking. The 29-year-old has certainly been open, and Cousins may be the perfect passer to actually get him the ball. I predict that Jennings finds new life and scores at least one touchdown against his former team on Sunday night. 3. Sunday's matchup is only the beginning of what's to come This may already be the NFL’s game of the year. The well-balanced 49ers against the blitz-happy Vikings is a matchup made for the primetime stage. But who says this has to be their only meeting? In fact, if both teams continue on their current paths, a late-round playoff matchup may be an inevitable sequel. We simulated the rest of the season using PFN’s NFL Playoff Predictor. 🔮 Here’s the projected playoff bracket 👀 pic.twitter.com/QBo8zogNJ6 There’s a lot of football to be played, and neither team is in the easiest of divisions, but these are two squads built for postseason success. You may need to bookmark this one, but I predict that Sunday will not be the last time we see Minnesota and San Francisco battle this year. Whoever takes round two may end up having Valentine’s Day plans at SoFi Stadium. picks.headline: Sportsbook Insiders: Insights on Vikings vs. 49ers Odds for Sunday Night Football; Kirk Cousins Impact
picks.blurb: Sportsbook Insiders: Insights on Vikings vs. 49ers Odds for Sunday Night Football; Kirk Cousins Impact Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins has transformed the NFC playoff picture since being traded from Las Vegas to Minnesota at the trade deadline, and that’s set up a very interesting Sunday Night Football matchup in Week 11. The Vikings are set to face the San Francisco 49ers in a neutral site game in Mexico City, and there are a ton of playoff implications at stake. Not only are the Vikings battling for first place in the NFC North, but a win over San Fran would give Minnesota a legit shot at the No. 1 seed in the conference. A Cousins trade materialized for Minnesota after back-to-back losses to Detroit and Buffalo where Kyler Murray (against Detroit) and Carson Wentz (against Buffalo) showed that they simply aren’t playing quarterback at a high enough level for the Vikings to win a Super Bowl. That sentiment has changed in the futures market, as the Vikings are now priced around 15/1 to win it all after an upset win over Green Bay in Week 10. The odds for that game shifted in a big way after Cousins was acquired, as the same goes for Week 11 against San Francisco. Sports Illustrated spoke to several oddsmakers this week to see just how much the Cousins’ acquisition has changed the Vikings’ outlook in this Sunday Night matchup. How Much Kirk Cousins Impacts Vikings vs. 49ers Odds for NFL Week 11 The Vikings opened as 3.5-point underdogs in Week 11 after their win over Green Bay, but that line has continued to move towards the Vikings, settling at 3. While that’s a minor move, there’s a chance this line would have been set as far as 49ers -7 if Murray or Wentz was under center on Sunday night. “Well, if the quarterback play continued to go the way it was before Cousins arrived, the Vikings would have been close to a touchdown underdog, rather than a field goal underdog,” Johnny Avello, Director of Race and Sports Operations for DraftKings Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. That’s at least a four-point swing in favor of the 49ers, though not every book had that price. BetMGM and FanDuel both told Sports Illustrated that the spread would likely be close to four or five. “Not too much believe it or not, probably was about a point or so move,” Christian Cipollini, Senior Trading Manager at BetMGM , told Sports Illustrated. The reason being is there isn't a major gap between Cousins and Murray. The main reason for this spread being close is the strength of the defense. Both QBs are capable, it helps Minnesota's future odds more because if one gets injured they have a capable backup to come in.” It’s interesting to hear about different pricing across the industry, as Fanatics has a much different grade – but similar to DraftKings – when it comes to the Murray vs. Cousins debate: “We opened up a lookahead line on the day of trade deadline day, it was plus seven,” Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. “And now the Vikings are three-point dogs, just to give you an idea of how highly we rate Kirk Cousins versus Murray or Wentz.” In his first start with the Vikings, Cousins threw for 207 yards, two scores and one pick, and he has 22 touchdown passes in the 2026 season. There’s no doubt that this Vikings team – which has the No. 2 defense in EPA/Play in 2026 – has a much better chance of competing with San Fran’s No. 1 offense with Cousins calling the shots. What Would the Vikings vs. 49ers Spread Be in San Francisco? This game is also unusual because of the neutral site aspect. away.blurb: While last week's victory over the Green Bay Packers for the Minnesota Vikings centered around the return of quarterback Kirk Cousins, it's easy to forget that the win was also achieved without Jordan Addison, Blake Cashman, and T.J. Hockenson on the field. After first announcing that Addison would be heading to short-term injured reserve , Minnesota changed its mind, and the 24-year-old receiver isn't expected to be out of action for as long as many initially believed. On Friday , Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said the veteran quarterback is "definitely getting close" to returning to practice, but because he is an "explosive mover" when he plays, the team wants to get him as close to 100 percent healthy as possible before clearing him to return. Isaiah Rodgers - CB (Questionable) Minnesota starting corner Isaiah Rodgers was added to the team's injury report on Thursday after sustaining a quad injury in practice. Rodgers still took part in all three of the Vikings' practices this week, but he was a limited participant on Thursday and Friday due to the injury. Bengals vs. Commanders odds, expert picks, and our prediction for Week 11 matchup
