That culminated in an absolute whooping of the Pittsburgh Steelers at home on Sunday Night Football that wasn't even as close as the 20-point win made it seem. Now they are taking their show on the road to play the Washington Commanders in their house on Monday Night Football. Joe Burrow is 0-2 so far in his career against the Commanders, but that comes with some pretty big caveats. The first loss was the game in which he injured his knee midway through the game as a rookie. The other loss came in an absolute monster of a shootout where the Bengals defense did not stop the Commanders or Jayden Daniels a single time in 2024, with the game ending 38-33. That would not be the first time Burrow would helm a losing team despite putting up more than 30 points over the next few seasons. These teams are drastically different as the Cincinnati defense has had a major overhaul, and Washington is far from the team it was during Daniels' rookie season. There is no doubt Daniels is a talented quarterback, but the Commanders themselves seem to be a very average to below-average team that needs a combination of home run hits on offense and a handful of turnovers to spark a win. Meanwhile, Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins are giving their best impressions of the Colts' offense during Peyton Manning's heyday by trusting their quarterback to put up points with his top weapons over a balanced attack. That has led to four straight games of four touchdowns for Burrow, which ties a record set by Manning. The real x-factor here will be the Bengals defense. Will the version we have seen since the Madrid game against the Atlanta Falcons show up that has been able to contain opposing offenses that tried to test their linebackers and safeties? Or will the young players at those positions allow a few too many big plays? Here is how the oddsmakers and experts feel about the game. The Bengals are currently 6.5-point road favorites against the Commanders, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . It really is a fairly big deal when a road team gets almost a touchdown advantage over a home team. It clearly shows that there is a step between where these two teams are currently at. The point total is set at 53.5 is the second highest of the week. That is fair because even when this team has faced teams like the Tennessee Titans, they have given up opportunities to score. 10 of ESPN's 11 experts are going with the Bengals CBS Sports has all seven experts taking Cincinnati to win All five of NFL.com's experts are expecting the Bengals to extend their win streak to six games NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from across the web — has Cincinnati receiving 99% of the picks for this game. Cincy Jungle Pick I think this team has really turned a corner as far as this defense is concerned. The young linebacker duo of Demetrius Knight and Barrett Carter have grown enough to prove to be a competent — maybe not the most consistent — duo. That is the level of play this defense needs when the defensive line led by Boye Mafe and Dexter Lawrence is able to get penetration. We will have to see how well they contain Daniels, who can really cause some damage by extending plays with his legs. All of that more or less will determine how much the Commanders lose by. Washington has no way of slowing down or throwing off this offense. The Bengals are getting into at least the 30s. Can the Commanders keep pace? Final Score: Bengals 45, Commanders 25 Who Dey! away.blurb: The Bengals are keeping decent health rolling following the second practice of Commanders week, but illness is hanging around. Dalton Risner's (knees) status for Monday's game got hazier after sitting out a second consecutive practice this week. Dylan Fairchild (oblique) logged another limited session today and is trending in the right direction to play. Kyle Dugger (quad) was a full participant on Friday. Bengals Injury Report: Dalton Risner's Status Gets Murkier Following Latest Practice Skip to main content SI.COM Joe Burrow logged another full practice as he fights through that illness, and Dax Hill is also under the weather. Hill didn't practice on Thursday or Friday. Cincinnati is trying to parlay their five-game winning streak into a six-game run. Burrow's league-leading play in basically every major passing category has been the biggest catalyst. "He's just on it," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said about his quarterback on Sunday. "I thought the protection was really good. There are some times that they are going to create some movement, but it's blocked movement. I think Joe did an excellent job keeping his eyes down the field and finding guys for some big plays. Those guys made big plays and tremendous catches — all of those guys really. Everyone stepped up and made some plays for us. Obviously, he (Burrow) set the tone. "This is just how he is. I feel like I've seen him in this rhythm quite a bit. He has a lot of confidence. Like I've said before, the offensive line is blocking so well that it allows us to play confidently. At one point we had 24 passes and six runs. It is what it is. As long as these guys are doing that and we are making our way, that's how it's going to be." Burrow isn't counting any chickens before they hatch; it's not even Thanksgiving yet, as plenty of work remains. "Yeah, we're clicking right now, but as I said, seven wins certainly isn't going to do anything for you. Nobody's winning championships in Week 9. It's a big win, but we've got a long way to go," The star passer said after Sunday's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh. Cincinnati has a light practice tomorrow before traveling on Sunday.
